title: Leeds’ Daniel Farke banned and fined for confronting officials after Manchester City loss
content:
Leeds United manager Daniel Farke has been handed a one-match ban and fined following his sending off at full time of his side’s loss to Manchester City on Saturday.

Farke, 49, was shown a red card by referee Peter Bankes after jogging onto the Elland Road pitch and confronting the match officials following the 1-0 defeat.

The Leeds manager was sanctioned with misconduct by the Football Association (FA), and after admitting the charge, was handed the standard one-game suspension plus an £8,000 fine.

His behaviour was a breach of Law 12 in the International Football Association Board’s (IFAB) laws of the game, which state it is a red card offence to enter the field of play to confront an official.

The ban means Farke will not be in the dugout for Sunday’s FA Cup fifth-round tie against Norwich City at Elland Road.

Farke gave an 11-minute answer when asked about his sending off during his pre-match press conference before Tuesday’s defeat to Sunderland.
